name: RW Cam
description: A Cepheid in the Milky Way that pulsates every 16.42 days; its mean radius is 97.5 solar radii.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, RW Cam: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 97.5 +/- 7 (Monte-Carlo)

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 136, Name='RW Cam', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 5125 +/- 253 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic)

distance.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, RW Cam: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 1967.8 +/- 139.7 (Monte-Carlo)

color.reason: Interstellar dust reddens every spectrum of this star, E(B-V) = 0.633 +/- 0.016 (Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10), and its light changes through each pulsation

text.card: A Cepheid in the Milky Way, 98 times the Sun's width, that swells and shrinks every 16.4 days.
text.introduction: Its mean radius, 97.5 solar radii, comes from comparing how fast its surface moves with how its size changes, 1,968 parsecs away.
text.locator: table10, RW Cam: Per, Rad, Dist

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius.
No dynamical mass is measured for this Cepheid; its mass is left unmeasured.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 473043922712140928 (quality A), from 2024A&A...690A.246T; Gaia DR3 measures none
